children: said personal data on about 11mn customers, employees and others across its group companies may have been exposed in a cyberattack,
reported on November 25. The company traced the possible breach to an intrusion it detected in September.

Keio, one of the Tokyo area's main railway companies, disclosed in September that ransomware had struck a server belonging to a group company. It said at the time that outside specialists were helping it determine how much data might have been compromised. The disclosure on November 24 was its first estimate of the number of people affected.

The company said the possible leak covered sensitive identity and payment records. Subsidiaries including Keio Plaza Hotel Co held passport numbers and passport copies that may have been taken, and credit card numbers held by Keio Department Store may also have been exposed.
Keio said copies of My Number cards, Japan's national identification documents, may have leaked from Keio Realty & Development Co and other group firms.

The company confirmed that names, addresses and other details of about 12,000 people had been exposed. That group includes current and former staff of Keio and its subsidiaries, as well as people who had applied for jobs there.

The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) separately disclosed a breach on the same day. It said intruders had gained unauthorised access to its system for distributing Earth observation data. Account names and encrypted passwords belonging to about 2,000 users were leaked.
The platform supplies weather and precipitation data gathered by observation satellites. It has been offline since November 18, and the agency has not said when service will resume.
According to JAXA, the attackers got into the system through a flaw in its software and installed a backdoor.

title: Japan's Keio says cyberattack may have leaked 11mn records
